headline_marked: Jamaat Ameer: [[BNP government is walking the path of autocracy]]
headline: Jamaat Ameer: BNP government is walking the path of autocracy
summary: Dr. Shafiqur Rahman warns that the 11-party alliance's eight-point demands could turn into a 'one-point' demand for the government's resignation.
details: Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Dr. Shafiqur Rahman has accused the BNP-led government of moving toward autocracy by ignoring the verdict of a referendum. He made these remarks during a road rally in Tangail's Nagar Jalfai bypass area as part of a long march from Dhaka to Rangpur.

The Ameer stated that the government has deceived the nation and vowed that the opposition parties will continue to work to ensure the people's rights. He warned that if the July Charter and other demands are not met, the alliance will launch a movement based on a single-point demand.
NCP convener Nahid Islam, also speaking at the rally, claimed that one autocrat has been replaced by another and warned that this government's fate would be the case of the former fascist regime.

LDP Chairman Colonel Oli Ahmed (Retd.) added that the opposition is not against the government itself, but against the government's shift away from reforms. He noted that if this trend continues, the opposition will be forced to move toward a one-point demand.

The 11-party alliance's long march began with an opening assembly at Manik Mia Avenue in Dhaka. The march will include seven public meetings and five road rallies across Dhaka, Gazipur, Gazipur, Tangail, Sirajganj, Bogura, Gaibandha, and Rangpur, concluding with a final assembly at the Rangpur Zila School field.

headline_marked: Within 100m of police station: [[Mugging of rickshaw passenger in Chattogram]] goes viral
headline: Within 100m of police station: Mugging of rickshaw passenger in Chattogram goes viral
summary: Two men on a battery-run auto-rickshaw robbed a passenger of their phone and cash in broad daylight, just meters away from a police station.
details: A mugging incident occurred in Satish Babu’s Lane in the Patharghata area of Chattogram, reportedly between 6:30 am and 7:30 am.
A viral video recorded from a nearby house shows two young men on a battery-run auto-rickshaw blocking a pedal rickshaw to commit the robbery.
The attackers forcibly took a mobile phone and cash from the passenger's pocket and quickly fled the scene on their vehicle.
Police sources confirm the spot of the robbery took place within 100 metres of the Kotwali Police Station.
Despite the viral video, no formal complaint has yet been filed with the police station in connection with the incident.
Habibur Rahman Pramanik, deputy commissioner (South) of Chattogram Metropolitan Police
told The Daily Star, that several teams are working on the case and they are searching for the victim to catch the robbers.
